portInfo.description: Cozumel is a western Caribbean staple known for reefs, beach clubs, and downtown San Miguel. Ships normally dock at one of three piers—Punta Langosta, Puerta Maya, or International Pier—rather than tendering. Check your daily program for the assigned pier before planning a walk into town.
portInfo.timezone: Eastern Time (UTC−5 year-round in Quintana Roo)
portInfo.language: Spanish; English widely spoken in tourist zones
portInfo.currency: Mexican peso (MXN); USD often accepted in tourist areas

facts.established: Historic Maya coastal links; modern cruise piers south of San Miguel
facts.significance: One of the Caribbean’s highest-volume western itinerary ports
notableFeatures: Puerta Maya and International cruise piers
Beach clubs along the west coast
culturalHighlights: Fresh seafood and Mexican coastal cuisine
East-coast wild beaches on island tours

size.portCapacity: Multiple cruise piers handling frequent multi-ship days
size.annualVisitors: Among Mexico’s busiest cruise islands (see APIQROO / destination statistics for current season totals)

climate.averageTemp: Warm to hot year-round; highs often upper 20s–low 30s °C
climate.rainySeason: Summer wetter with storm risk; dry season is peak cruising weather
climate.humidity: High—hydrate between pier and beach club
climate.description: Dry season brings the most reliable beach weather. Summer heat and humidity make exposed walks from southern piers into town less appealing than a taxi.

politics.stability: Tourism zones are accustomed to cruise volumes; follow local and cruise-line guidance
politics.visaRequirements: Mexican entry rules depend on nationality. Many visitors complete a tourist permit/FMM process via airline or on arrival—confirm current rules with official Mexican immigration sources and your cruise line.
politics.entryRequirements: Carry a valid passport and follow ship instructions for going ashore. Pier shopping zones are not a substitute for checking re-boarding cutoffs.

gettingThere.fromTerminal: Cozumel uses three main cruise piers—Punta Langosta (downtown), Puerta Maya, and International Pier (south of town, near each other). Confirm the assigned pier on your ship’s daily program; line patterns exist but are not guaranteed.
gettingThere.distanceToCity: Punta Langosta: waterfront downtown. Puerta Maya / International Pier: typically a few kilometres south of San Miguel (often ~10 minutes by taxi in light traffic)
gettingThere.walkingTime: Easy from Punta Langosta. From Puerta Maya / International Pier, walking to downtown is long and hot—taxis are the usual choice
gettingThere.taxiInfo: Fixed-rate taxi boards are common—agree destination and rate before departure
gettingThere.publicTransport: Limited urban transit for visitors; most independents walk near downtown or taxi to beaches/ruins. Tendering is uncommon and usually only when pier capacity or operations require it.

thingsToDo.intro: Cozumel has three main cruise piers. Your assigned pier (posted on the daily program) changes whether downtown is a walk or a taxi.
topThings: San Miguel waterfront shopping and dining
Beach clubs along the west coast
Snorkeling or diving on Cozumel’s reefs
East-coast wild beaches on a guided island loop
thingsToDo.shortCall: From Punta Langosta, walk downtown. From Puerta Maya or International Pier, taxi to a nearby beach club or into San Miguel—then return with time to spare.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Beach club + light downtown time, or a focused snorkel trip, fits most calls. Island-wide east-coast loops need an earlier start.
thingsToDo.longerCall: Ruins + beach, or a longer reef outing, become realistic. Still confirm pier assignment before assuming you can walk into town.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Puerta Maya and International Pier sit near each other south of town; Punta Langosta is the downtown pier. Tendering is uncommon and usually only when pier capacity or operations require it—follow ship instructions.
